headline: Chip Names Lead a Broadly Higher Tape as Storage Stocks Crater
body_html:
Stocks are holding firm through midday Friday, with 376 names in our universe trading higher against 163 in the red — a lopsided advantage that has the tape tilted decisively to the upside. Semiconductors are the engine, posting a sector gain of roughly 4.3% and pulling the broader market along with them. Industrials and Materials are also running, up 1.6% and 1.3% respectively, while Software and Homebuilders are lagging in minor negative territory.

The standout movers inside the semiconductor complex tell a nuanced story. Life-sciences tools firm Azenta is the session's top performer, up nearly 16%, followed by connectivity chipmaker Synaptics at nearly 14% and MaxLinear at nearly 12%. Semiconductor-equipment names Veeco Instruments and Axcelis Technologies are also surging, adding 11% and 8% apiece. The gains are wide and deep within the sector. On the other side of the ledger, storage hardware is under severe pressure: Seagate Technology has shed more than 14% and Western Digital over 13%, a pair of declines sharp enough to constitute a sector-specific warning flag.

Into the close, traders will be watching Treasury yields, which are inching higher as the market awaits a key jobs report. Geopolitical tension — Iran's posture, Houthi activity in Yemen, and OPEC+ uncertainty — adds a ceiling to any energy-related optimism. Position sizing ahead of the weekend will be the final test of conviction in today's rally.

briefs.headline: Storage Hardware Hit by Double-Digit Losses
briefs.body: Seagate Technology and Western Digital are among the steepest decliners in the session, shedding 14.5% and 13.2% respectively. The simultaneous selloff suggests sector-specific pressure rather than a company-level event, and traders are watching whether the pain spreads to adjacent technology names before the close.

briefs.headline: OPEC+ Shelves Capacity Review as Iran Conflict Reshapes Supply Calculus
briefs.body: The oil producers' alliance has postponed a scheduled review of member production capacity after the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict upended expansion planning, according to sources cited by Reuters. Energy stocks are up about 0.9% on the session, though the delay introduces fresh uncertainty about medium-term supply commitments.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Edge Up Ahead of Jobs Data
briefs.body: Government bond yields are ticking modestly higher as investors position for a closely watched employment report. Analysts note that internal bond-market signals may suggest the recent sell-off is losing momentum, but conviction remains low until payroll figures are in hand.

briefs.headline: Iran Signals Escalatory Response if Attacked, Dimming Diplomatic Hopes
briefs.body: Iranian authorities have indicated preparedness for a more forceful military response should the country face further strikes, with Reuters reporting that diplomatic channels face long odds of success. The development keeps a geopolitical risk premium embedded in energy and defense-related market segments heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Nike Drops Nearly 6%, Weighing on Consumer Sector
briefs.body: Nike fell almost 6% on Friday, making it the steepest decliner among consumer names and one of the worst performing in the broader market. The Consumer sector is clinging to a gain of just 0.2% for the session, underscoring how much Nike's drop is acting as a drag on the group.

briefs.headline: Freight Name RXO Surges Alongside Industrials Rally
briefs.body: RXO Inc climbed more than 8% in Friday trading, standing out within an Industrials sector that is up roughly 1.6% on the day. The freight-brokerage company's move adds to a pattern of logistical and industrial names outperforming as investors rotate toward economically sensitive areas of the market.
